headline: BlackRock chief executive Larry Fink said a broad freeze on new data centres could push the United States into recession.
score_reason: Pool score kept: on-record claim from the head of the world's large asset manager on a live election issue; the recession link is his view.
importance_line: The debate touches households facing higher power bills, local officials weighing projects and investors in AI infrastructure, but Fink runs a firm that invests in data centres, and the recession link is his claim.
summary: Larry Fink, chief executive of the asset manager BlackRock, told CNBC on Wednesday, after BlackRock's third-quarter results, "If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession," and called most criticism of data centres "misinformation." The remark comes as data centres become a campaign issue before the 3 November US midterm elections, over electricity bills, water use and limited visibility into financing.
notes: CNBC original not read; BigGo Finance relays the interview. BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners recently completed a roughly $40 billion Aligned Data Centers deal (BigGo), which is the conflict-of-interest context.
